Before you commit Begin with the boundary before choosing the panel A boundary project is partly a building decision and partly a neighbour conversation. In Queensland, the Neighbourhood Disputes (Dividing Fences and Trees) Act 2011 sets a process for adjoining owners considering a sufficient dividing fence . That does not mean every premium material, extra height or preferred finish is automatically shared. Establish the line and the intended standard before comparing prices. Start with a written description of the work and at least one quote. If discussion does not settle the matter, a notice to contribute is the formal step and the timing matters: the government process allows one month to reach agreement, followed by a possible QCAT application within the stated period. Treat this as general information, not a promise about the result or a substitute for checking the current Queensland guidance. General information as at July 2026. The current rules are published by the Queensland Government and dividing-fence disputes are heard by QCAT .
